title: Data Structures and Algorithms: Main Exam, December 2019
programme: Bachelor of Science in Information Technology / bachelor of Business Information Technology
instructions: ANSWER QUESTION ONE AND ANY OTHER TWO QUESTIONS

parts.text: Define the term algorithm.
Outline four characteristics of a good algorithm.
Explain the function of the following ADT primitives. Write the relevant syntax.
Enqueue()
Push()
IndexOf()
One of the applications of stacks in computing is to evaluate a postfix expression. From the given expression 5+4*6-3:
Convert the expression into a postfix expression.
Using the stack ADT, show how the expression will be evaluated.
A queue is implemented using an ADT list to present its items. Discuss the efficiency of the queue insertion and deletion operations when the ADT list implementation is:
Array based
Pointer based
Outline four possible applications of the ADT queue in computing.
In the context of arrays, explain the term index. Show an example.
Using examples, differentiate between a binary tree and a general tree.
Write a two-dimensional array to explain the concept of row major order.
Explain two types of complexities studied in data structures.
Given the algebraic expression (a-b/c)+d*e:
Convert it into a postfix expression.
Generate a binary tree from the expression.
Give three reasons why you would choose a linked list over an array.
Name and explain three input cases and the effect on the running time of an algorithm.
Describe the concept and motivation of a circular queue. Use an illustration.
In terms of computational complexity, using big O, explain the cost of:
Inserting an element at the end of an array list.
Inserting an element at the end of a linked list.
Write down the algorithm for inserting a new element into a stack.
Define the term "algorithm analysis". Explain two important quantitative metrics of interest in algorithm analysis.
Sort the array 30, 20, 6, 15, 8, 3, 4 using the insertion sort algorithm.
Explain three characteristics of the ADT linked list.
Using an illustrative diagram, show how a new element is added in between other elements in a linked list.
Explain two data types used to implement ADTs.

Perform pre-order, in-order and post-order traversal on the following tree. The root is D, with left child E and right child Z. E has a left child K, and K has a right child P. Z has a left child C and a right child M. C has a left child B and a right child F.
Discuss five benefits of studying data structures and algorithms by software developers.
